lines.trans: There is always such a big line here.
They make the most delicious pastries in town here!
Do you know that people often propose here?
This is the first time I hear about this.
The town registry office is right nearby.
And what do you want to say by that?
Samson, what is this lying in my pastry?
This is a beautiful gold ring for you!
Samson, have you completely lost your mind?
You and I have been together a whole month.
I have a separate room in a communal flat.
Marry me right now!
No, Samson, I do not agree.
Take this ring back for yourself.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('tasty, delicious').

examples.trans: The bread rings are very tasty.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, присядьте. Попробуйте чай с сушками, очень вкусные.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, have a seat. Try the tea with bread rings, they're very tasty.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'together' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.
examples.trans: Pasha and I have been together for a month now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.trans: She's offended. She's always like that.

выходить.gloss: to go out, to get out

meanings.en: to go out, to come out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go out, to get out', paired with 'выйти'.

examples.trans: I'm going out in a minute.

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'town, city' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.
He is the chairman of the city court.
We walked in the city park.

examples.text: Председатель городского суда. Илья Олегович Берг.
examples.trans: The chairman of the city court. Ilya Olegovich Berg.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.

examples.text: Я уже не могу готовить, стирать, убирать. Я хочу на море!
examples.trans: I can't take the cooking, washing and cleaning any more. I want to go to the sea!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?
We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

забрать.gloss: to take back, to take away

meanings.en: to take away, to pick up
meanings.note: забрать заявление = to withdraw a statement
забрать заявление = to withdraw a statement

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.en: civil registry office (for marriages and births)
meanings.note: acronym treated as a masculine noun

examples.text: Тут же рядом находится городской ЗАГС.
examples.trans: The town registry office is right nearby.

examples.text: Теперь мы вместе пойдём в ЗАГС.
examples.trans: Now we will go to the registry office together.

meanings.note: used with verbs like выходить for marriage of a woman

examples.trans: He asked me to marry him and come to Moscow!

examples.text: Она вышла замуж в прошлом году.
Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
He's very good with his hands.

examples.text: Товарищ генерал, операция называется Золотой ярд.
examples.trans: Comrade General, the operation is called Golden Yard.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
Watch. I'm taking off my ring.

meanings.note: colloquial for коммунальная квартира: one flat shared by several families

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
We live in a communal flat.

examples.text: Детство у меня было трудное. Я вырос в коммуналке.
examples.trans: My childhood was hard. I grew up in a communal flat.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('beautiful, handsome').

examples.trans: They have a very beautiful house.

meanings.en: to lie, to be lying down, to rest

examples.text: Такие люди должны лежать в особенном месте!
examples.trans: Such people should lie in a special place!
The book is lying on the table.
But I'll be lying next to Grishka for eternity.

meanings.note: уже месяц = for a month now

examples.trans: I've been living here for a month.
The election is in a month.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.
examples.trans: Pasha and I have been together for a month now.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

находиться.gloss: to be located, to be found

meanings.en: to be located, to be situated

examples.trans: Where is the operating room located?
The town is situated on a river.
Where is the operating room located here?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
+ prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ратно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Afterwards I'll drive you back for free.

examples.text: Вот это дело! Потом обратно бесплатно отвезу.
examples.trans: Now we're talking! Afterwards I'll drive you back for free.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'дельный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('separate').

examples.text: У меня есть отдельная комната в коммуналке.
examples.trans: I have a separate room in a communal flat.

examples.text: У меня есть две отдельные комнаты.

meanings.note: стоять в очереди = to stand in a queue; без очереди = jumping the queue
с первого раза = the first time

examples.text: Ты не понимаешь с первого раза?
examples.trans: You don't understand the first time?

examples.text: Ты что, с первого раза не понимаешь?
examples.trans: What, you don't understand the first time?

meanings.note: substantivized neuter adjective; declines like an adjective

examples.text: Пойдём, может, кофе с пирожным выпьем?
examples.trans: Let's go, maybe we'll have coffee with a pastry?

examples.text: Она купила к чаю свежие пирожные.
examples.trans: She bought fresh pastries for tea.

meanings.note: у меня есть предложение = I have an offer

examples.trans: It's a good offer, of course.

examples.text: Значит, предложение такое. Ты мне говоришь, где твои сорок миллионов.
examples.trans: So, here's the offer. You tell me where your forty million is.

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?
A plot next to Grigory Soprykin.
Right nearby, round the corner, there's a cheburek café.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
Do you know the main thing?

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

examples.text: Как странно, я ничего об этом не слышал.
examples.trans: How strange, I've heard nothing about it.

examples.text: Я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: No, Vika, that's not what I mean at all.

meanings.note: almost always the short form: я согласен (man), я согласна (woman)

сойти.gloss: to get off; (с ума) to go mad

meanings.en: to get off, to step down
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ойти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get off; (с ума) to go mad', paired with 'сходить'.

meanings.en: сойти с ума = to go mad, to lose one's mind

examples.trans: What, have I lost my mind?

examples.text: Позвонить Третьякову? Я что, с ума сошёл?
examples.trans: Call Tretyakov? What, have I lost my mind?

meanings.note: the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order
the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order

examples.text: То есть просто стоять и смотреть?
examples.trans: So we just stand and watch?

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: сойти с ума = to go mad, lose one's mind

examples.text: Позвонить Третьякову? Я что, с ума сошёл?
examples.trans: Call Tretyakov? What, have I lost my mind?
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

examples.text: Я не могу гулять здесь целый день.
examples.trans: I can't walk around here all day.
We waited for a whole hour.

examples.text: Илья Олегович! Я не могу гулять здесь целый день.
examples.trans: Ilya Olegovich! I can't walk around here all day.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: О, это, Аркашенька, бывает очень часто.
examples.trans: Oh, that happens very often, Arkashenka.
We often meet in the park.
I used to come see you often.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
